sourcedFrom: PSA AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — AR Family Users Manual, 44pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in the book. (UNDATED — nothing in the document states one)
cleanIntro: A direct-impingement AR strips in four moves: safety on, magazine out, rear takedown pin, upper hinged open. The bolt carrier group and the charging handle come out the back, and PSA publishes two steps past that — the carrier group itself, and the buffer tube, where the action spring is waiting under compression.

steps.title: Safety to SAFE before anything else
steps.action: Put the safety selector on SAFE first, with your finger off the trigger and the muzzle pointed somewhere that would not matter. On an AR the safety can only be set with the hammer cocked, so if it will not rotate, the hammer is down — cycle the action and try again rather than forcing it.
steps.quote: Place the safety selector on SAFE
steps.cite: PSA AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — AR Family Users Manual, 44pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in the book. — FIREARM SAFETY — Unloading The Firearm, p.20-21

steps.title: Magazine out, and pull it DOWN
steps.action: Hold the grip with your finger clear of the trigger, press the magazine release and pull the magazine down out of the well. Do this before you touch the charging handle: running the action with a loaded magazine in just chambers the next round.
steps.quote: Press the magazine release button and pull the magazine down to remove.
steps.cite: PSA AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — AR Family Users Manual, 44pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in the book. — FIREARM SAFETY — Unloading The Firearm, p.20-21

steps.title: Bolt locked open on the bolt catch
steps.action: Pull the charging handle fully to the rear, press in on the LOWER portion of the bolt catch to hold the bolt back, then release the charging handle. The lower paddle is the lock; the upper one releases.
steps.quote: Unlock and pull the charging handle all the way out [figure 3] and press in on the lower portion of the bolt catch [figure 4]. Release the charging handle. This locks the bolt in the open position.
steps.cite: PSA AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — AR Family Users Manual, 44pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in the book. — FIREARM SAFETY — Unloading The Firearm, p.20-21

steps.title: Look into the chamber through the ejection port
steps.action: With the bolt held open, look through the ejection port into the chamber and confirm there is no cartridge in it. A finger in the chamber settles what a glance into a shadowed receiver cannot.
steps.quote: Look into the receiver through the ejection port and verify that there are no cartridges in the chamber [figure 5].
steps.cite: PSA AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — AR Family Users Manual, 44pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in the book. — FIREARM SAFETY — Unloading The Firearm, p.20-21

steps.title: Glasses on — everything past here is under spring load
steps.action: Eye protection goes on before the takedown pin moves. The action spring in the buffer tube is compressed the whole time the rifle is together, and it is the part that reaches your face if the buffer retainer gets away from you later.
steps.quote:
! WARNING! Always wear eye protection eve-
ry time before handling your firearm for clean-
ing and maintenance.
steps.cite: PSA AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — AR Family Users Manual, 44pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, p.27

steps.title: Rear takedown pin pushed through, and it does not come out
steps.action: Push in the takedown pin above and behind the safety lever on the left side, then pull it from the right until it stops. It is captive — it will not come free of the receiver, so do not lever at it looking for a loose pin.
steps.aside:
You may then pull the pin from the right side
of the receiver until it stops (it will not pull out) [Figure
16]
steps.quote:
Step 2: Takedown Pin. Push in the takedown pin, located above and to the rear of the safety lever on
the left hand side of the receiver [figure 15].
steps.cite: PSA AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — AR Family Users Manual, 44pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, p.27

steps.title: Upper hinged open on the front pin
steps.action: Grasp the rear of the upper receiver and lift, letting it pivot on the front pin. That opens the rifle far enough for the bolt carrier group to come out and exposes the fire control group underneath — which is a good moment to notice how much carbon is in there and how little of it you should be poking at.
steps.quote:
Step 3: Separating the receiver. Grasp the rear of the
upper receiver and pull up, allowing it to pivot on the
front pin. This will expose the fire control group.
steps.cite: PSA AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — AR Family Users Manual, 44pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, p.27

steps.title: Bolt carrier out, then the charging handle down and back
steps.action: Pull the bolt carrier straight back until it clears the charging handle and the upper. Then pull the charging handle back to its stop, drop it down out of its channel and withdraw it to the rear. That order matters: the handle cannot leave the receiver until it reaches the cut that lets it drop.
steps.quote:
Step 4: Removing the BCG. Pull the bolt carrier
straight back until it is free of the charging handle and
upper. Pull the charging handle back until it stops,
then allow it to drop down to clear the upper receiver
and remove it from the rear.
steps.cite: PSA AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — AR Family Users Manual, 44pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, p.27

steps.title: Chamber first, with a chamber brush — and leave it DRY
steps.action: Scrub the chamber with a chamber brush and solvent or CLP, then patch it until the patches stay clean, then run one dry patch through. Do not oil the chamber: a wet chamber grips a fired case and raises pressure on the next round.
steps.quote:
After cleaning,
run a dry patch through the chamber. Do not oil the chamber.
steps.cite: PSA AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — AR Family Users Manual, 44pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in the book. — MAINTENANCE, p.31

steps.title: Barrel from the chamber end, patch until one comes out clean
steps.action: Push a solvent-soaked patch through from the CHAMBER end, then the brush several times to lift copper and powder fouling, then patches until one exits clean. Finish with a lightly oiled patch to protect the bore, and clean the outside of the barrel with a nylon brush.
steps.quote:
Using a cleaning rod, pass a patch soaked in bore cleaner through the barrel several times
starting from the chamber end.
steps.cite: PSA AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — AR Family Users Manual, 44pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in the book. — MAINTENANCE, p.31

steps.title: Carrier: lubricate the OUTSIDE only
steps.action: Clean the bolt carrier group with CLP or a suitable solvent and wipe the excess off before it goes back together. PSA is explicit that the inside of the carrier is not lubricated — oil in there collects carbon and turns into the paste that seizes a bolt. The exterior of the carrier is what gets the lubricant.
steps.aside: Lubricate the exterior of the carrier only.
steps.quote:
Be sure to remove
excess oil from the bolt assembly before reassembly, do not lubricate the inside of the carrier.
steps.cite: PSA AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — AR Family Users Manual, 44pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in the book. — MAINTENANCE, p.32

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retaining pin out, firing pin to the rear
deepSteps.action: Push the bolt assembly into the carrier until it stops, then take out the firing pin retaining pin and slide the firing pin out of the rear of the carrier. The retaining pin is small and the firing pin drops free once it is gone — do this over the bench, not over the carpet.
deepSteps.quote:
Step 1: Push bolt assembly (A) into carrier B until it
stops. Remove firing pin retaining pin (E) and slide
firing pin (F) to the rear of the carrier until it is free.
deepSteps.cite: PSA AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — AR Family Users Manual, 44pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in the book. — Bolt Carrier Group Disassembly, p.29

deepSteps.title: Cam pin quarter-turned, then straight out
deepSteps.action: Turn the cam pin a quarter turn so its head clears the gas key, then pull it straight up and out. It only comes out at that one orientation, and the bolt cannot leave the carrier until it does. ⛔ It also must go back: PSA warns that a rifle will still fire without the cam pin installed and may explode.
deepSteps.aside: Be sure the cam pin is installed in the bolt group. If it is not installed, your firearm can still fire and may explode causing injury or death.
deepSteps.quote:
Step 2: Turn Cam Pin 0 1/4 turn to allow the head of Figure 19
the pin to clear the gas key, and pull straight out.
deepSteps.cite: PSA AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — AR Family Users Manual, 44pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in the book. — Bolt Carrier Group Disassembly, p.29

deepSteps.title: Bolt out of the carrier — that is the end of the group
deepSteps.action: With the firing pin and cam pin out, the bolt assembly slides forward out of the carrier. Clean the bolt, the gas rings, the extractor and the inside of the carrier's bore; PSA publishes nothing deeper for an owner, so the extractor pin stays where it is.
deepSteps.quote:
The bolt assembly may now be removed from the
carrier assembly.
deepSteps.cite: PSA AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — AR Family Users Manual, 44pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in the book. — Bolt Carrier Group Disassembly, p.29

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Buffer tube: the action spring is compressed RIGHT NOW
deepSteps.action: Before touching the buffer retainer, understand what is behind it: the action spring is under compression and the retainer is the only thing holding the buffer in. Eye protection is not optional for this step and PSA says so on the page.
deepSteps.quote:
! WARNING! Action spring is under
compression. Please wear eye protection when
removing the buffer and buffer spring.
deepSteps.cite: PSA AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — AR Family Users Manual, 44pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in the book. — Buffer Tube Disassembly, p.30

deepSteps.title: Retainer down, buffer eased FORWARD under control
deepSteps.action: Press the buffer retainer pin down while holding the buffer back, then let the buffer travel forward SLOWLY once it clears the retainer — do not let it go. Once the spring is no longer compressed, draw the buffer and spring out of the tube and clean inside it with a cotton patch and CLP.
deepSteps.aside:
You may now clean the inside of the buffer
tube with a cotton patch and CLP.
deepSteps.quote:
Step 2: Push down on the buffer retainer pin [Figure
24] while holding the buffer back. Allow buffer to
travel forward slowly after clearing the retaining pin.
deepSteps.cite: PSA AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — AR Family Users Manual, 44pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code is printed anywhere in the book. — Buffer Tube Disassembly, p.30

cleaning.name: CHAMBER
tasks: Chamber brush with solvent or CLP, several passes
Patch until the patches stay clean
⛔ Finish with a DRY patch — the chamber is not oiled

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Solvent patch from the chamber end, then the brush, then patches until clean
One lightly oiled patch to preserve the bore
Outside of the barrel with a nylon brush and cleaner, then wipe

cleaning.name: BOLT CARRIER GROUP
tasks: Strip per the deep-clean steps; CLP or a suitable solvent
Carbon off the bolt tail, the gas rings and the extractor
⛔ Lubricate the EXTERIOR of the carrier only — never inside it

cleaning.name: UPPER, LOWER & BUFFER TUBE
tasks: Wipe the upper's interior and the locking lug recesses
Brush the fire control group area clean without disturbing it
Cotton patch and CLP inside the buffer tube

reassembly: ⛔ Cam pin FIRST, and prove it: bolt into the carrier, cam pin in and turned back a quarter turn under the gas key. A rifle assembled without it can still fire and may explode — PSA's own words.
Firing pin in from the rear, then the firing pin retaining pin back through the carrier.
Buffer spring and buffer into the tube, pressed back past the retainer until the retainer springs up in front of the buffer.
Charging handle into its channel from the rear, pushed forward until it seats.
Bolt carrier group in behind it, then run both forward together into the upper.
Close the upper onto the lower and push the rear takedown pin fully home.
Function check before any live ammunition.
fncheck: Reassembled, magazine out, safety on SAFE, muzzle in a safe direction. Charge the rifle by hand several times and watch the bolt lock and unlock — it should run without drag and the bolt should go fully into battery. With the hammer cocked, check the safety blocks the trigger; then, safety off, that the trigger releases and resets when the action is cycled. Confirm the takedown and pivot pins are pushed fully home. If anything binds or the bolt does not close, stop and get it looked at rather than firing it.
